violations: audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/chain/chain_check_results.json (committed at HEAD, written by commit 4b93bb5) contains a caveat string for the C.chi_top-vs-D.chi link that reads '...depends on declared input resolution_local_model (tier L)...'. chain_check.py:243 does a verbatim `d_status_note = D_exports.get("status")` and formats it with %r at chain_check.py:259-262. D-tda/exports.json:13's 'status' field has been fixed since commit d5f8301 (the ONLY commit that ever touched that file) at '...depends on declared inputs (local model of a resolved point)' -- a DIFFERENT string. chain_check.py's format-string code at this line has likewise been unchanged since commit 2dded2a. Since neither the input file nor the reading code has changed since before the JSON was committed, a byte-for-byte rerun of the committed chain_check.py against the committed D-tda/exports.json MUST reproduce the committed chain_check_results.json exactly -- and it does not (verified by clean-clone rerun; the ONLY diff in the entire file is this one line). This means the committed chain_check_results.json was not actually produced by running the final, committed chain_check.py against the final, committed D-tda/exports.json: it is stale (most likely generated once when D-tda/exports.json's status field briefly read differently, then D-tda's file was edited without chain_check.py being rerun before the chain commits were made). Rule 10 requires results.json to be reproducible from the stated command against the committed inputs; this one line is not. Severity: HIGH -- it is exactly the class of defect ground rule 10 exists to catch, and it survived three chain-track commits (d19c5d6, 2dded2a, 4b93bb5) without being caught.

audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/C-lattices/results.json rigidity entry for parameter_inserted='chi_top' is labelled RIGID_GIVEN_DEFINITION, but its own fields read: solution_set='chi_top=24 unique given the declared inputs (it is a computation, not a scan)', negative_control='none realizable... not a control; labelled HYPOTHETICAL and not counted', control_perturbs_same_parameter=false. Ground rule 8 defines RIGID_GIVEN_DEFINITION as 'RIGID once named defining inputs are granted', and RIGID itself requires 'a structural selecting condition ... and a neighbouring value demonstrably fails'. This entry admits there is no scan, no selecting condition over candidate values, and no realizable negative control -- by its own words it is a straight-line formula evaluation (chi(O)=h0-h1+h2, then x12 via Noether), not a selection process at all. It therefore does not meet ANY of the rule-8 categories that require a demonstrated failure mode. The correct label is CONDITIONAL_ON_INPUT (a value fixed once the K3 definition -- K=O, b1=0 -- is granted, with no rigidity test performed), matching the label already correctly used two entries later in the same results.json for the 'typed Gram 3U+2(-E8)' entry which is honestly self-labelled CONDITIONAL_ON_INPUT with selecting_condition='none (typed)'. File: audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/C-lattices/results.json (rigidity[1], id-less entry with parameter_inserted='chi_top'); also audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/C-lattices/03_merge.py (writes this classification). Severity: MEDIUM -- a labelling defect, not a numeric one; chi_top=24 itself is correctly computed and correctly flagged elsewhere (in C1_chi_top's own 'note' and in the chain-check caveat) as depending on a typed Noether constant.

audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/B-dyons/results.json entry id='B5_margin' (script theta_margin_check.py) declares shared_inputs=['Jacobi_theta_definitions'] only. Reading theta_margin_check.py directly (lines ~28-34 of the clean-clone copy) shows it calls `knorm = Fr(load_inputs()['K3_elliptic_genus_factor_k']['value'])` and then `P2.compute(q1, QCHK-1, knorm, ...)` and `P3.run(q1, QCHK, 20, 60, knorm, Hh, ...)` where Hh is loaded from hurwitz_results.json. So B5's own computation depends on K3_elliptic_genus_factor_k (the declared k), on Hurwitz_H0/Kronecker_Hurwitz_relation (via the Hurwitz table it reads), on immortal_ansatz_form (via part3's ansatz), and on weak_Jacobi_ring_monomials (via part2's basis) -- none of which appear in B5's declared shared_inputs. Rule 7 requires 'every result lists shared_inputs: the names of the declared inputs it depends on', and this propagation is incomplete. Severity: LOW-MEDIUM -- B5 is a stability/margin cross-check (QMAX 40 vs 60 agreement), not itself a headline numeric claim, but a reader trusting the shared_inputs field to audit dependency propagation (as rule 7 intends) would be misled into thinking this check is nearly input-free.
